- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment spikes) — reduce forecast peak values.
- Underestimate prices during prolonged negative sentiment — adjust downward bias by 2–5% relative to recent mean.
- Overshoot after sharp upward spikes — cap forecast at 1–2% below prior peak or 1–3 days lagged high.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 14-day moving average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- Sentiment-driven lag: if sentiment is negative for 3+ consecutive days, delay forecast peak by 1–2 days and reduce magnitude.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts overestimate early in negative sentiment cycles — reduce first 5–7 days by 3–5%.
- Avoid “sentiment echo” — if sentiment is negative but forecast is bullish, reduce forecast by 5–10% to match sentiment drift.
